title: Gas Rates, New Sign Rules, Taxi Fares, City Upgrades
summary:
*   **Gas Franchise Under Fire**: A major public hearing saw strong opposition to Southern Union Gas Company's proposed changes, including new definitions for gas, altered service extension policies, and increased fees. Decisions were postponed due to public and City Attorney concerns.
*   **New Sign Regulations Spark Debate**: A comprehensive ordinance aimed at updating sign rules, particularly impacting real estate and commercial signage, faced scrutiny from businesses. The proposed changes, including amortization for existing signs, led to a delay in final adoption.
*   **Taxi Fares Climb, Service Expected to Improve**: Taxi rates were increased (e.g., 70 cents for the first 1/4 mile), and permit fees rose, while charges for extra passengers were eliminated. This move aimed to stabilize the struggling taxi industry.
*   **Investing in City Infrastructure & Services**: Over $1 million was approved for 18 new transit buses, along with significant appropriations for Brackenridge Hospital upgrades and parking. The city also pushed forward with essential utility projects and explored sites for a new Senior Citizen Center.

service. He stated that the new Wrecker Ordinance prevents this type of operation with
respect to collision rotation calls in that the sign that identifies the permit holder has

and efficient service.

on the door. However, Mr. Cortez suggested that one main permit holder be listed with any

that the problem presented by Mr. Cortez was one of concern.

as more body shops get out of the wrecker business and did not think the problem would be
solved.
City Attorney Don Butler stated that this was strictly a policy decision for the Council
and felt the ultimate issue involved was whether one wrecker service was going to be on
the rotation list several times just because it has contracts with several different
entities. 41

IMPROVEMENTS TO BROOKE ELEMENTARY SCHOOL
The Council had before it a report on the requested improvements to the Brooke Elementary
School Playground. MR. MIKE SEGREST, Assistant Director of Parks and Recreation
Department, noted that an evaluation was made concerning this situation at Brooke
Elementary School and referred to the report that was presented to the Council. By use of
